what_happened: The job to run the test check with cargo-nextest failed in planning. After three rounds the critic still said "revise" and no code was written. The critic confirmed the plan's main claims about the code and said the files outside the reading's list were justified. It raised one major finding. The wrapper looks for the pinned nextest under athena_home(), but checks run with a cleared environment that has no ATHENA_HOME or XDG_DATA_HOME. On a machine that sets either one, the check would quietly fall back to plain `cargo test`, with no speedup and a wrong after-median. Nothing in the plan would notice. There were four minor findings. Three said checks.rs, gh.rs and config.rs are not in the reading's deliverables. One said the plan lets an unverified CI pin land, although criterion 3 asks for a checksum pin. One said the criterion 5 demonstration only tests the parsers and exit logic on sample output, not a real nextest run of the test check.
cause: Planning does not check what environment a step will really run in. Checks run with a cleared environment, and a plan can assume variables or install locations that are not there. A fallback to the old command also looks like success, so nothing shows the new path never ran. The plan has no step that makes the new behavior observable, such as reporting which runner was used. The reading also left out files the change must touch, and it did not require a verified pin. So the critic kept finding gaps through round 3 and the job ran out of rounds.
prevention: Add a planning rule and a critic check for any plan that changes how checks or CI run a tool. First, the plan must state the exact environment the step runs in (the check env allow-list, HOME and PATH) and show where each path or variable it needs comes from. Second, any fallback must either fail loudly or print which path it took. Third, the demonstration must run the real check end to end and show the tool's own output, not only parsers on sample text. Also let the reading list the code files a change needs, such as the check runner, the gh helper and the config schema, so the scope critic does not raise them. Make the pin checksum a hard requirement in the plan, not an allowed deviation.
proposed_request: Run the test check with cargo-nextest to cut suite run time. Outcome: the `test` check in Athena runs the suite through a pinned cargo-nextest, and CI and the local check give the same pass or fail result as `cargo test`. Deliverables: the wrapper and install step in xtask, the check runner (crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs) so it counts tests from nextest output, crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs so it still finds the failing test name, the config schema (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs) and athena.toml for the tool pin, and the CI workflow. Acceptance: (1) The check runs in its cleared environment, which has only HOME, PATH and the fixed list. The plan must show how the wrapper finds the pinned nextest there. Set ATHENA_HOME from {athena_home} in the capability env for change and study, and do not rely on XDG_DATA_HOME. (2) The wrapper reports which runner it used. If nextest is missing it fails the check with a clear message and does not fall back to `cargo test`. (3) The nextest pin has a verified checksum, and the plan must not allow an unverified pin to land. (4) The test count and failing test name are parsed correctly from nextest output, and libtest output still works. (5) Demonstrate by running the real `test` check once. Show that it ran nextest, how many tests it counted, and the before and after medians for suite time. Keep CI routing unchanged with one `test` check.
